the production of MSSM charged Higgs boson in association with the lightest neutral Higgs boson and the production of two neutral Higgs bosons at the LHC are promising channels to probe the Higgs sector in the nondecouppling region.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LHC is sensitive to the MSSM H^\pm A^{0}, H^{+} H^{-} pair production signals in the entire low-m_A region, which is a crucial test of the MSSM Higgss sector in the non-decoupiling region.

H^\pm A^{0}, H^\pm h^{0} and H^{\pm}H^{-} signals would be observable at the LHC for a wide range of m_A and tan\beta, and thus, Higgs pair production is an ideal channel to probe the MSSH Higgs sector in the non-deoupling region.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the exploration for pair-produced MSSM Higgses at the 14 TeVCollider is a crucial next experiment to probe the MSSMs.

the exploration of H^\pm h^{0}, H^\pm A^{0}, and H^{\pm}H^{-} production at the Lhc would provide a powerful probe for the MSSM Higg sector, and would be complementary to the study of the H\pm and H^\pm A^\pm channels at the ILC.

H^\pm A^{0} and H^{+}\!H^{-} production can be observed at the LHC with a modest amount of integrated luminosity, and the discovery reach for these channels can be extended to a much higher mass scale than the other Higgs production channels.
